subject: GreenHaven Labs — private deployment runbook and VPC review
messages:
From: Ava Singh <ava@greenhaven.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@greenhaven.io
Date: 2028-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment kickoff — network checklist + preferred cutover windows

Hi Markus / Camila / Grace,

Thanks for the intro — excited to move our private deployment forward. We've finalized procurement for the on-prem package and want to lock down network requirements and a short implementation timeline. High level asks:

- Confirm VPC peering constraints (e.g., cross-account peering vs transit gateway).
- Private endpoint needs (Kafka, internal telemetry endpoints) and required ports.
- On-prem appliance shipping ETA and contact for receiving PO.
- A short preflight call next week to walk the network diagram and NAT/egress expectations.

Attached is our current VPC CIDR list and the signed PO for the on-prem package. Can you confirm the minimum subnets we should reserve and any routing rules that Redwood requires?

Attachments: [attachment: greenhaven_vpc_cidrs.csv (text/csv)], [attachment: GHL-OnPrem-PO-#4512.pdf (application/pdf)]

Preferred preflight windows: Nov 6 (10–12 PT) or Nov 7 (13–15 PT). Let me know if either works.

Thanks,
Ava Singh
Senior Infrastructure Lead
GreenHaven Labs

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Ava Singh <ava@greenhaven.io>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network checklist + preferred cutover windows

Ava — thanks for the details and the PO. We've pulled together a first-pass runbook and a set of minimum networking requirements. Key notes up front:

- For predictable latency and to minimize blast radius we recommend a direct VPC peering per account (no shared transit gateway for initial rollout). We can revisit TGW for multi-account scaling later.
- Required outbound egress: 443 to our control plane, and a small set of IPs for telemetry (see runbook). If GreenHaven requires explicit allow lists, we'll provide the stable IP set.
- Private endpoints: we support internal HTTPS endpoints for model inference and a separate metrics endpoint. We'll need the internal DNS zone and whether you'll use Route53 inbound endpoints or a forwarded DNS resolver.
- On-prem appliance: shipping address/receiver + preferred receiving hours required for carrier SLA. The PO looks good; I'll have Ops provide the packing list and serial numbers once the order is queued.

I've attached a Redwood runbook stub that outlines the implementation steps and the minimal CIDR/reservation guidance. Please review and we'll iterate on the network diagram in the preflight call.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preflight — Nov 6 10:30 PT (we'll send a calendar invite).
2) Customer to confirm DNS plan + VPC CIDRs to reserve (reply with any changes to attached CSV).
3) Redwood to share a short list of IP egress addresses and a proposed peering diagram.

Attachment: [attachment: redwood-runbook-v1.0.md (text/markdown)]

—Markus Klein
Director, Customer Implementation
Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Ava Singh <ava@greenhaven.io>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, netops@greenhaven.io
Date: 2028-11-01T13:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network checklist + preferred cutover windows

Ava — jumping in with the implementation run cadence and checklist we'll follow during the preflight and staging phases.

Quick summary of what we'll cover on the call:
- Network diagram review (VPC peering, route table expectations, NACLs vs SGs)
- Private endpoint mapping (inference, metrics, admin API) and port/ssl expectations
- KV cache sizing + expected token throughput for initial tenants (to inform MTU and keepalive settings)
- On-prem appliance setup: power/rack/SSH-access requirements and serial console plan for our support team
- Shipping contact and PO handling (we'll confirm ETAs after Ops acknowledges the PO)

If NetOps prefers a transit gateway (they mentioned TGW in a prior note), please bring the preferred TGW account/principal to the call so we can validate Resource Access Manager (RAM) or peering permissions.

I added a short preflight agenda to the runbook and will share an editable diagram prior to the call.

—Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Singh <ava@greenhaven.io>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@greenhaven.io
Date: 2028-11-02T08:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network checklist + preferred cutover windows

Thanks — Nov 6 10:30 PT works for our NetOps and cloud team. A couple of clarifications before the call:

- We intend to use TGW in the long term, but for security signoff we'll allow a temporary per-account peer for the initial rollout. NetOps prefers TGW but will bring the RAM principals on Nov 6.
- Attached is an updated CIDR file (minor change: 10.12.32.0/20 instead of /21 for their analytics VPC).
- Shipping contact is: Ethan Ross, Facilities Manager — ethan.ross@consultnet.com — loading dock receives shipments M–F 07:30–16:00 PT. Tracking and ASN should be emailed to ethan.ross@consultnet.com and ava@greenhaven.io.

Attachments: [attachment: greenhaven_vpc_cidrs_v2.csv (text/csv)]

We'll plan for a hard preflight checklist completion by Nov 9 so we can schedule an initial staging cutover the week of Nov 13.

Cheers,
Ava

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Ava Singh <ava@greenhaven.io>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, netops@greenhaven.io
Date: 2028-11-03T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff — network checklist + preferred cutover windows

Ava — appreciate the quick turnaround and the shipping contact. Summary / action items from Redwood:

- We will run the preflight on Nov 6 10:30 PT (calendar invite sent).
- Redwood to provide: peering diagram + conservative egress IP list by EOD Nov 2 (posted to runbook link).
- GreenHaven to confirm final CIDRs in the shared CSV by EOD Nov 4.
- Redwood Ops to acknowledge PO and provide packaging/serial numbers once the order is queued (target: Nov 7).
- Prep checklist completion target: Nov 9; first staging cutover window: week of Nov 13 (TBD during preflight).

I'll open an implementation Jira (SUP-1203) for tracking and will attach the runbook and the diagrams to the ticket. If anyone prefers a different tracking tool, reply with the ID and we'll consolidate.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Grace O'Connor
Implementation Program Manager
Redwood Inference
